sum: Optional extra for PC players. Linking your 24-character account ID keeps your ranks, star chart, syndicates and quests in sync on any device. Adding an inventory file fills in what the ID can't see: the gear you own, blueprints and parts, mods, arcanes, relics, resources and your Foundry. The easiest way to get that file is WFHelper.

other: Warframe on PC (Windows; Linux works too)
WFHelper, a free open-source desktop companion (wfhelper.com)

steps.t: Download WFHelper from wfhelper.com (or its GitHub releases page, github.com/WFHelper/WFHelper/releases) and install it.
steps.tip: It's an open-source community app. It isn't made by Tennoform or Digital Extremes.

steps.t: Start Warframe and log in until you're standing in your Orbiter. Leave the game running.
Open WFHelper. In its first-run setup, pick warframe-api-helper (recommended) as the inventory source. On Linux the same option is called Read from the running game.
steps.tip: Already set WFHelper up with another option? Change it in WFHelper's Settings.

steps.t: Wait until WFHelper shows your inventory. That means it has saved inventory.json and codex-profile.json on your PC.

In Tennoform, open Profile, then Account & sync. Under Add your full inventory, tap Choose file. Click the file window's address bar, paste %appdata%\WFHelper\api-helper and press Enter, then pick inventory.json.
steps.tip: On Linux the folder is ~/.config/WFHelper/api-helper. If you pointed WFHelper at your own copy of warframe-api-helper, inventory.json sits next to that program instead.

steps.t: Check the summary. If something looks wrong, tap Undo last import to put everything back.
Repeat after a play session whenever you want fresh numbers. WFHelper keeps inventory.json up to date while it runs, and each import replaces your relic, resource and Foundry counts.

fast: Pin %appdata%\WFHelper\api-helper in your file window's Quick access, and re-importing takes two clicks.
Not linked yet? Pick codex-profile.json from %appdata%\WFHelper under Link your Warframe profile; it holds your account ID.
Sign in to Tennoform first, so the imported progress syncs to your phone and other devices.
was: AlecaFrame keeps its own copy of your inventory, but it's encrypted, so that file can't be uploaded here. Use a tool that saves a plain inventory.json instead.
Tennoform will never ask for your Warframe password. Don't give it to any site or tool.
Running warframe-api-helper on its own often fails to download the inventory now. WFHelper runs it for you and retries, and can also read the game directly, so use WFHelper.
Tools that read the game's login session aren't officially approved by Digital Extremes. Using any third-party tool is at your own risk; Tennoform itself never touches the game.

sum: Your account ID is a 24-character code made of the numbers 0–9 and the letters a–f. Tennoform uses it to read your public profile (ranks, mastered gear, star chart, syndicates, quests) and keep it synced. It isn't a password and can't be used to log in. Warframe doesn't let sites look it up from your in-game name, but warframe.com knows it while you're logged in, and one click reads it from there.

steps.t: Log in at warframe.com with the account you play on (any platform). In Tennoform, Account & sync has an Open warframe.com button for this.

Computer (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari): in Tennoform's Account & sync, tap Copy the console line. On warframe.com press F12 (Mac: Cmd+Option+J; Safari needs Develop menu turned on), open the Console tab, paste and press Enter. You land back in Tennoform; tap Link this account.
steps.tip: If Chrome or Edge says pasting is blocked, type allow pasting, press Enter, and paste again. The line only reads your account ID from warframe.com's own login cookie.

steps.t: Computer, one-click version: drag the Tennoform ID button from Account & sync to your bookmarks bar. Next time, click it while on warframe.com.

Android (Chrome): tap Copy the bookmark in Account & sync. Tap ⋮ then ☆ to bookmark the page, then Edit the bookmark: name it Tennoform ID and replace its address with what you copied. On warframe.com (logged in), type Tennoform ID in the address bar and tap the bookmark in the suggestions.
steps.tip: Tapping it from the bookmarks list doesn't run it in Chrome; it has to be picked from the address bar.

steps.t: iPhone or iPad (Safari): tap Copy the bookmark. Tap Share, then Add Bookmark, save it, then open Bookmarks, tap Edit, pick it, rename it Tennoform ID and replace the address with what you copied. On warframe.com (logged in), open Bookmarks and tap Tennoform ID.
On PC with WFHelper: open "Use WFHelper on PC? Pick its files instead", tap Choose WFHelper file, paste %appdata%\WFHelper into the address bar, press Enter and pick codex-profile.json.
steps.tip: The file appears once WFHelper has loaded your inventory at least once.

steps.t: Using a web inspector (desktop dev tools, or an inspector app on iPhone)? On warframe.com, logged in, open the Resources or Application tab, then Cookies. Open user-info and copy the 24 characters after "user_id":". Paste them into Account & sync.
steps.tip: Don't use _gsid. It's 32 characters long and is a Google Analytics ID, not your Warframe account.

steps.t: Already know your ID? Paste it into the box under Already have your ID? and it links straight away.

fast: On a computer the console line takes about 15 seconds; the bookmark is one click after that.
Once linked, your profile re-syncs by itself; you only do this once per device, or once in total if you're signed in to Tennoform.
was: The account ID is not the same as your in-game name (alias) or your platform's user name. It's always exactly 24 characters, using only 0–9 and a–f.
warframe.com/api/user-data used to show the ID as plain text. That page now returns a 404 ("Ordis" error page), so Tennoform reads the ID from warframe.com's login cookie instead.
Warframe's EE.log used to show your ID on a "Logged in Name (ID)" line. Current logs only say "Logging in as Name", without the ID.
There's no way to look up an account ID from an in-game name. Warframe removed that in update 38.0.8.
Only run console lines you trust. Tennoform's line is shown in full before you copy it in Account & sync; it reads one cookie and sends you back here, nothing else.

The _gsid cookie on warframe.com looks like an ID but isn't: it's a 32-character Google Analytics session ID. Your Warframe account ID is the user_id inside the user-info cookie, always 24 characters.
